lines.say: Meiosis makes gametes: sperm and eggs, pollen and ovules.
One diploid cell divides twice, giving four haploid cells.
It halves the chromosome number, and it creates variation.
First, DNA is copied in interphase. 46 chromosomes, 92 chromatids.
Prophase one: homologous chromosomes pair up side by side. That's synapsis.

draw.alt: A homologous pair side by side: maternal and paternal chromosomes, each with two chromatids

lines.say: Non-sister chromatids touch at chiasmata and swap sections. Crossing over.

draw.alt: Non-sister chromatids swap their bottom sections, making recombinant chromatids

lines.say: Metaphase one: the pairs line up on the equator, in pairs.
Anaphase one: homologues are pulled apart. Sister chromatids stay joined.
Two cells, each already haploid. 23 chromosomes, 46 chromatids.
No DNA copying in between. That's how the number halves.
Metaphase two: chromosomes line up one by one, not in pairs.
Anaphase two: centromeres split. Sister chromatids go to opposite poles.
Four haploid cells, each with 23 chromosomes and 23 chromatids.
In females, only one large egg forms. The small polar bodies break down.
Variation comes from three things, like a deck of cards.
Cut: crossing over in prophase one makes new allele combinations, like A with little b.
Shuffle: each pair lines up randomly at metaphase one. Independent assortment.

draw.alt: Two homologous pairs line up two ways, giving four gamete combinations

lines.say: Combinations equal 2 to the power n. For humans, 2 to the 23 is about 8.4 million.
Deal: random fertilisation. Any sperm can meet any egg.
Variation is what natural selection acts on.
Mitosis: one division, two identical diploid cells.
Meiosis: two divisions, four different haploid cells.
Only meiosis pairs homologues and crosses over, in prophase one.
Non-disjunction is when chromosomes fail to separate. Like handouts stuck together.
One gamete gets an extra chromosome, n plus 1. Another misses one, n minus 1.

draw.alt: Chromosomes fail to separate: one gamete gets two copies, the other gets none

lines.say: An error in anaphase one affects all four gametes.
An error in anaphase two leaves two normal gametes.
An n plus 1 gamete fertilised gives trisomy, like trisomy 21.
Crossing over is between non-sister chromatids, not sister chromatids.
Cells are already haploid after meiosis one.
Meiosis one splits partners. Meiosis two splits sisters.
Use the haploid number in 2 to the n. 2n equals 8 gives 16.
